journey.name: Restore — a recovery phrase, and three honest answers when it fails
journey.description:
The third door. Before this, a user who had a pubky but whose Pubky Ring was on a lost or dead phone had no route back into Loopky at all.
Most of what matters here is the failure copy, because the three ways this goes wrong are genuinely different and collapsing any two of them lies to someone who is already anxious about having mistyped. A checksum-passing typo is the common case, and it derives a *valid* phrase that simply is not theirs — calling that "invalid" sends them hunting for a problem that is not there. A DHT that cannot be reached is not a verdict on anything.
The phrase below is the standard BIP-39 test vector. It is public knowledge, so it is safe to type into a journey — but note it IS registered on staging, so it signs in rather than reporting "no account". Use a phrase you have altered by one word to see the no-account path.

actions.action: From a signed-out Loopky, verify "onboarding_restore" is present and reads "Restore with a recovery phrase"
Verify "restore_seed_warning" is present, is NOT dismissible, and warns against entering a Bitcoin or crypto wallet phrase — it must be permanently visible above the field, not a toast
THE TYPO CASE. Enter a valid phrase with one word changed (e.g. replace the last word "about" with "abandon" — still a valid BIP-39 checksum). Tap "restore_phrase_submit"

Verify "restore_outcome_title" reads "That's not a valid recovery phrase" ONLY if the checksum failed; if the checksum passed, it must instead read "That phrase doesn't match an account" and NEVER call the phrase invalid
Verify "restore_outcome_pubky" shows the derived pubky — the user recognising it is not theirs is the fastest diagnosis available
THE OFFLINE CASE. Turn on airplane mode, edit one character, and submit again
Verify the outcome offers a retry and says "We couldn't check that" — it must NOT say the phrase is wrong or that no account exists
THE HAPPY PATH. Enter: abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon about
Tap "restore_phrase_submit" and verify Loopky lands on home (tab_study/tab_decks/tab_discover/tab_profile present)

Verify logcat shows exactly ONE "lookupHomeserver:" line for the attempt — the pre-flight answer is passed into sign-in, and asking the DHT twice costs ~3s on the only path back in for someone locked out
Settings → Sign out. Verify signing out succeeds (a restored key counts as backed up, since the user demonstrably holds the phrase they just typed)

LANDSCAPE. Rotate to landscape and re-open the onboarding screen. Verify "Restore with a recovery phrase" and the policy consent are reachable — the two-pane branch bounds the panel to the window height, and before #147 a third button clipped in silence with no error and no ellipsis
